subject: Request: Simplify telemetry/exports for OmniTrust POC (priority ask)
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-03T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Request: Simplify telemetry/exports for OmniTrust POC (priority ask)

Hi Irene / Ben —

Quick context: OmniTrust is in the final stages of a POC and they’ve made a gating ask around telemetry delivery. Their security team requires an automated nightly export of anonymized request traces and usage metrics to an S3 bucket + a small JSON summary pushed to our customer portal. This is blocking the POC signoff and, importantly, the commercial motion — the AE flagged this as a must-have for the contract we expect to close by month-end.

Why this matters:
- Account: OmniTrust (OT-2027-87) — ARR on close ~ $540k ARR, expected start-of-year ask for prioritized onboarding.
- Customer requirement: push daily zipped exports (logs + small metadata JSON) to a customer-owned S3 with field-level redaction (PII removal rules attached).
- Deadline: customer wants a canary by 2027-10-21 to validate.

Ask: can Product/Eng prioritize a small-scope feature to provide a configurable telemetry export adapter (S3 sink + redact transform) or provide an alternate low-friction solution we can ship within two sprints? Key constraints from customer: encrypted in-transit and at-rest, tenant-scoped exports (one file per tenant/day), and auditable delivery (manifest with checksums).

Attachments: OmniTrust_Security_QA.pdf (their security checklist) and OmniTrust_requirements_summary.xlsx.

Suggested minimum scope for MVP (to keep effort bounded):
- Enable a tenant-level export toggle in Console
- One export target type: S3 (customer bucket) with simple key prefixing and server-side encryption flag
- Simple redact pipeline: drop/email/hash fields based on a configured ruleset (rules provided by Omnitrust)
- Delivery manifest (small JSON) that lists files + checksums

If this exact scope is too large, please propose the smallest realistic workaround (e.g., a documented manual process, short-lived temporary credentials, or an export script we run for them) and an LOE. I can escalate timeline tradeoffs with the customer.

Thanks — appreciate a quick read and an LOE estimate.

— Laura Bennett
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
(415) 555-0198

[Attachment: OmniTrust_Security_QA.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: OmniTrust_requirements_summary.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-03T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Simplify telemetry/exports for OmniTrust POC (priority ask)

Thanks Laura — good summary. A few clarifying Qs so we scope correctly: 

1) Scale/volume: what is the expected events/day or average log size? (small POC vs prod-level ingestion changes the design).
2) Retention requirement and whether the customer expects Redwood to store the exported files for them or rely solely on their S3 copy.
3) Redaction: do they have a canonical list of fields to redact or do they want pattern-based rules (PII detectors)?
4) Access: do they want push-only (we write to their bucket) or pull (we expose URL they fetch)?

From an implementation POV we have two approaches:
- Fast path (2 sprints): a configurable export job that runs nightly, zips tenant keys, posts to an S3 bucket using a customer-provided role/credentials. Minimal transform: field whitelist/blacklist + hashing for obvious PII. No GUI work beyond a simple toggle and an ARN field.
- Full path (4–6 sprints): add streaming export + transformation, UI for rules, retries/manifest guarantees, and end-to-end audit trail in Console.

I can carve out a quick spike to validate the S3 push + manifest flow. Ben, can you provide a rough level-of-effort for the fast path (engineering hours / dependency list)? Also flag any security/privacy review items — we’ll need a quick legal/security signoff for writing to customer buckets and the redaction approach.

Irene
Product Manager, Redwood Inference

P.S. Related: see prior export RFC (internal link) — I can paste the doc in Drive if helpful.

[Quoted: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick context: OmniTrust is in the final stages of a POC and they’ve made a gating ask around telemetry delivery... ]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-04T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Simplify telemetry/exports for OmniTrust POC (priority ask)

Irene — quick answers from the customer call this morning (Samantha on the thread):
- Expected data volume (POC): ~2–3GB/day compressed, spikes up to ~6GB.
- Retention: they want the nightly export retained in their bucket for 90 days; Redwood does not need to keep a long-term copy (they want us to push only).
- Redaction: they provided a field list (PII columns) — attached in the QA PDF. Pattern-based detection is OK as fallback.
- Access: push-only preferred (we assume a role into their bucket).

Commercial ask: they’ll sign the SOW if we can demonstrate an automated nightly export canary by 2027-10-21. The legal/compliance gate is light if we use their bucket + ARN + attest to redaction.

If Product can commit to the fast path LOE, I’ll move this to a top-priority sprint and lock in a pilot engineers contact on the customer side. Customer contact: Samantha Cole <samantha@omnitrust.com>.

Thanks — Rishi
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-10-07T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Simplify telemetry/exports for OmniTrust POC (priority ask)

Brief LOE and plan from Eng:

Fast path estimate (aimed at canary by 2027-10-21): ~6 engineer-days (2 engineers, 1 week) + 2 days for infra/setup/config + 1 day for basic Console toggle. Total ~9 engineer-days (~1.5 sprint-days across a small squad). Work breakdown: 
- Export job: nightly batch job that aggregates per-tenant traces and metrics + zip + manifest generation (3 eng-days)
- S3 push integration using customer role (1 eng-day + infra)
- Redaction transform (config-driven whitelist/blacklist + hashing) (2 eng-days)
- Console toggle + minimal UI for ARN/manifest check (1 eng-day)
- Testing, e2e, and pilot run with OmniTrust (2 eng-days)

Dependencies / gating items:
- Security review sign-off for writing to customer buckets and the redaction approach (Priyom, can you expedite?)
- Access: we need an assumed-role or temporary creds from OmniTrust before we can run a live canary.
- SRE: small quota bump for nightly job I/O if they stick to 6GB/day spikes.

If Product signs off on the fast path scope, I’ll allocate the spike team and we’ll aim to land a canary pipeline. If we need richer UI/rule engine, that becomes a separate follow-up (4+ sprints).

I’ll attach a quick sketch of the export adapter and link a short Jira ticket to track (RW-4921).

— Ben Carter
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
